To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the smallest active form of human O6-alkyguanine-DNA alkyltransferase (MG MT) is 179 amino acid residues long, and the mutant MGMTs with conservative substitutions at the active site retain substrate binding and may be used for NMR studies.
the smallest active form of human O6-alkyguanine-DNA alkyltransferase is a protein with deletion of 8 residues at the amino terminus and 31 at the carboxy terminus.

(a) human MGMT, a 207-residue protein, is active as a monomer; (b) the smallest size of the protein that retains activity and binds to DNA is 179 residues; (c) the active site mutant proteins, which retain substrate binding, may be useful in determining the structure and mechanism.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the elucidation of the mechanism of the repair reaction by MGMT.
the elucidation of the mechanism of action of human O6-Methyl-guanine-DNA methyltransferases, which is the first step in the repair of O6-alkylation in DNA.
the development of new strategies for cancer treatment and prevention, and the elucidation of the mechanism of human O6-alkyguanine-DNA alkyltransferase.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the C145A mutant of MGMT has a specific and stable complex with the O6-alkylation substrate, but is inactive in repair.
the active site of human MGMT can be mutated without loss of substrate specificity and binding affinity, and that the mutant proteins can be used as tools to investigate the structure and mechanism.
MGMT has been engineered for structural and mechanistic studies by NMR, X-ray crystallographic, and other biophysical techniques.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
human MGMT is a monomeric protein with an active site cysteine at Cys-145 and that the protein is inactivated by a specific and stoichiometric reaction with O6-alkyguanine adducts in DNA.
we have developed a number of active site mutants and deletion mutants of MGMT that may be used for structural studies.
we are able to identify the smallest size of human MGMT which is active and forms a stable complex to the substrate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the C145S mutant of human MGMT can bind to a m6G-containing oligonucleotide and protect the DNA from digestion by DNase I.
the Cys145Ala mutant of MGMT retains the substrate specificity of the wild type protein.
the C145A mutant of MGMT is a useful reagent for footprinting studies of MGMT-DNA interactions.
